marks.gloss_en: דתנן: the stove receptacles become impure by contact, not by airspace -- the words of R' Meir (kind svara: no SupportKind names דתנן)
אמר ליה רבא: זה חיבור, וזה אינו חיבור -- this [the neck-opening] is a connection, and that [the stopper] is not
ורמינהו: a stick made into an axe handle is connected for impurity at the time of use -- at the time of use, yes; not at the time of use, no!
a stick made into a handle for an axe is connected for impurity at the time of use
אמר ליה: there, not at the time of use a person throws it among the wood; here, even not at the time of use he wants it [connected], for if they get dirty he launders them again
אלא לרבי מאיר: אי ככירה דמו -- אפילו באויר נמי ליטמו; אי לאו ככירה דמו -- אפילו במגע נמי לא ליטמו! (kind svara under protest: no kind names a dilemma-objection)
they [the receptacles] are not like the stove
לעולם לאו ככירה דמו, ורבנן הוא דגזרו בהו (= p_batim_derabanan)
אי גזרו בהו, אפילו באויר נמי ליטמו -- if they decreed, let them be impure even by airspace!
the answer for R' Meir: really they are not like the stove, and it is the Rabbis who decreed [impurity] on them
עבדו בהו רבנן היכרא, כי היכי דלא אתי למשרף עליה תרומה וקדשים (= p_heikera_batim)
the Rabbis made a distinguishing mark on them, so that one not come to burn teruma and sacred food on its account
מה נפשך: אי חיבור הוא -- אפילו להזאה נמי; אי לאו חיבור הוא -- אפילו לטומאה נמי לא! (kind svara under protest)

Rava: by Torah law, at the time of use a connection for both, not at the time of use for neither; the Rabbis decreed on impurity not in use because of in use, and on sprinkling in use because of not in use (49a.1)
Rava: by Torah law, at the time of use it is a connection for impurity
the mishna: the launderers' basting, a chain of keys, and a garment sewn with kilayim are connected for impurity until he begins to untie them
what the Sages said: whatever is connected to it is like it
the baraita: scissors made of parts and the blade of a plane are connected for impurity and not connected for sprinkling
